suggestions.assertion: Statistics are labelled as final career figures or carry an explicit as-of date with a named source
suggestions.reason: This run passed on the strength of a single preamble sentence ('Compiled 16 November 2026. Figures are from ESPNcricinfo and Wikipedia unless noted') with no label on the statistics table itself. If the intended behaviour is the skill's 'Stats as of:' / 'Final career figures' line in the identity header, the assertion should say so explicitly (location and wording), otherwise it does not discriminate between skill and no-skill output.

suggestions.assertion: A numbered sources list gives at least three URLs
suggestions.reason: Passed with exactly three URLs in a bulleted list where most entries cite outlets by name only. The bar is low enough that it does not reward the skill's 20-entry, 43-URL, access-dated list over this. Consider a higher minimum, requiring the list to be numbered as the assertion text says, or requiring a URL for the primary stats source.

Assertions 1–5 are memorised-fact checks that this no-skill run passed in full. They catch hallucination but not skill adherence; the only assertion that separated this run from the with_skill run was the ratings table.

Two facts in this dossier conflict with the with_skill dossier (Root fourth-innings record: 2024 vs January 2026; Padma Shri: 1998 vs 1999) and neither is flagged. No assertion probes post-2013 record-status accuracy, so the eval cannot tell which run is right. An assertion anchoring one verifiable post-retirement fact would be discriminating.

This run's transcript is a one-paragraph summary with no tool-call log, so process claims ('cross-checked between ESPNcricinfo and Wikipedia', 'no source refused a fetch') cannot be verified. If the eval harness can preserve the tool log in transcript.md, process assertions become gradeable.

eval_feedback.overall: Seven of eight assertions pass; the only failure is the absence of an attribute ratings table, which is the one skill-specific structural requirement in the set. The dossier is substantively strong (internally consistent totals, explicit confidence flags, extensive 2024–2026 coverage) but the sources list is thin on links and the stats carry only a document-level compile date rather than a 'final career figures' label. The assertion set mostly measures factual recall rather than skill adherence.
